title: Using a spoon to eat is a common skill by age two
summary: CDC's two-year movement list says the child eats with a spoon, beyond merely attempting one.
body: At the second birthday, CDC's movement checklist says the child eats with a spoon. The wording is eats, so the utensil is used to take food in, which is a step past merely attempting the spoon. The page does not add a neatness rule to that line. The publisher counts a milestone as something most children do by that age, and it defines most as 75 percent or more. Learn the Signs pages are issued by the National Center on Birth Defects and Developmental Disabilities, which states they cannot stand in for a validated screening instrument.
